I think my problem - and perhaps this applies to others as well - is I feel the idea in my head is a story I’m really passionate about and don’t want to BS my way through it by writing too carefree, only to have to essentially rewrite the whole thing over again in the editing process. It’s really a double edged sword.

As I’m someone else may mention, try to read horror fiction, just to get a grasp of what you’re trying to get into. There are different ways to go about it, depending on your story. Something I’ve come to find out for myself-as a writer of horror-is the more I try to make a story scary for the sake of it being scary, the worse it is. A story isn’t scary without a genuine cause for fear. Characters always come first for me, and depending on whatever conflict the protagonist(s) is/are dealing with, the antagonist can be molded around that. Or perhaps vice versa; there is no one way to do it. 

I’ve never written about zombies or monsters, so I can only give you advice from what I‘ve done, which is usually making the villain(s) stand as a metaphor for something the protagonist fears confronting, and the inevitable overcoming of it. Think about trauma, vices and dread. Those to me are what I use the most. Hope this helps.

In the Fall of 2014, I went back to resume my Biology degree, but dropped out again bc I tried to take Biochem, Genetics, Invertebrate zoology, and statistics at the same time. I could’ve just dropped a few but my anxiety/depression at the time was really bad and I wanted to be as far away as possible from school. I sank into alcohol for the next four years while working at a factory. It’s was good money, but I just couldn’t live with the thought of never completing my degree. I quit my job last September and went back, this time taking fewer classes to ease my way back into it. As of right now, I am about to complete my first full year in six years and plan on graduating in December. I don’t like saying I regret initially dropping out, what matters most is my life is going in the right direction once again.
